claims.text: The api Deployment has 2 replicas and keeps the default RollingUpdate strategy (maxSurge/maxUnavailable 25%), so it adds one new Pod, waits for it to be ready, removes one old Pod, and repeats; old and new Pods serve side by side until the rollout ends.

claims.text: A revert restores manifests, not data: applied migrations stay, so the previous version comes back against the newer schema.
claims.source_hint: devops.l3.rollback-by-revert summary line 5; Argo CD docs, hooks (no Down is run on revert)

claims.text: Zero-downtime migration: a schema change made while the system keeps serving, so each migration works with the code before and after it. Expand and contract: add the new shape beside the old, move the code, remove the old once no running version uses it.

dotnet ef migrations add writes a migration from changes to the mapped model, compared with the model snapshot, and updates that snapshot. At stage-3 it scaffolded two DropTable calls, deleted by hand, so Up is empty and only the snapshot records the new mapping.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs, Migrations overview / Managing migrations (model snapshot); PaymentsAndNotificationsLeaveOrdering.cs @ stage-4 lines 7-25

claims.text: DropOldNotificationsTable is the contract step, step 2 of ADR 0008; Up calls DropTable(name: "notifications"); the api of the previous release no longer reads or writes the table, so an old Pod cannot fail on a missing table.

The rows were dumped first by scripts/backend/drop-old-notifications.sh (ADR 0008 step 1, pg_dump -Fc --table); the old payments table stays until accounting confirms its check against donhang_payments (step 3).

claims.text: Trade-offs: one migration with its code breaks old Pods and reverts; stopping the api costs a planned outage and still leaves the revert problem; expand and contract keeps both versions working at the cost of extra releases.
Dropping the old payments table is compatible for the code (no code reads or writes it) but should wait for accounting's confirmation, step 3 of ADR 0008.

To rename customers.email while serving: add nullable contact_email with code writing both; once no older Pod is left, copy email into rows lacking contact_email; move reads; drop email in a release whose previous version no longer touches it. If a short outage harms nobody, stopping is simpler.
